extracted.intended_audience: Surface Transportation Board staff; California High-Speed Rail Authority; transportation and environmental counsel; cooperating agencies; stakeholders and members of the public participating in STB rail construction exemption proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures the Surface Transportation Board uses to decide whether to grant exemptions under 49 U.S.C. 10502 for rail construction projects, including evaluation of transportation merits, NEPA and NHPA (Section 106) compliance, mitigation requirements, and procedural deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption standard under 49 U.S.C. 10502
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 10502(a), the Board must exempt a proposed rail line construction from the prior approval requirements of section 10901 when it finds that (1) those procedures are not necessary to carry out the rail transportation policy of 49 U.S.C. 10101, and (2) either (a) the proposal is of limited scope or (b) the full application procedures are not needed to protect shippers from an abuse of market power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory two-part test the Board applies to decide whether to grant an exemption rather than requiring a full 10901 application. The decision explains the Board's reliance on this standard and cites past decisions applying it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public convenience and necessity standard under 49 U.S.C. 10901(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 10901(c) directs the Board to grant authority for a rail line construction proposal unless it finds the proposal 'inconsistent with the public convenience and necessity.' There is a statutory presumption that rail construction projects are in the public interest and should be approved unless shown otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing transportation merits, the Board treats approval as presumptive absent evidence showing inconsistency with public convenience and necessity; challengers must present evidence to overcome the presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation policy considerations (49 U.S.C. 10101 factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: In applying 10502 and 10901 standards, the Board examines how the proposal aligns with the rail transportation policy in 49 U.S.C. 10101, including reduction of Federal regulation, development of a sound rail system with effective competition, fostering sound economic conditions in transportation, reducing regulatory barriers to entry, encouraging energy conservation, and addressing health and safety impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision lists specific policy objectives (e.g., 49 U.S.C. 10101(2), (4), (5), (7), (14), (8)) and explains that the Board found the project furthers those objectives; absence of contrary evidentiary showings supports reaffirmation of earlier conclusions on transportation merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening proceedings standard — new evidence and changed circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will reopen previously decided dockets when a petitioner provides new evidence and demonstrates changed circumstances that warrant reopening the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Authority's petitions to reopen were granted because the Board found new evidence and changed circumstances (e.g., supplemental environmental analyses) sufficient to justify reconsideration; reopening triggers solicitation of comments on merits and fresh review of supplemental environmental/historic materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA substantive requirement — identify and evaluate environmental effects
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA requires Federal agencies to examine the environmental effects of proposed major Federal actions and to inform the public concerning those effects; agencies must consider significant potential beneficial and adverse environmental impacts and may authorize, deny, or condition actions based on that analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEPA prescribes the process (scoping, Draft/Final EIS, public comment) but not a particular result; once environmental effects are adequately identified and evaluated, the agency may conclude other values outweigh environmental harms. The Board relies on NEPA analysis in deciding whether to authorize construction or impose mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS adequacy standard — compliance with CEQ regs and 49 CFR part 1105
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental Impact Statements (Draft and Final Supplemental EISs) must adequately assess potential environmental impacts and meet the standards of the Council on Environmental Quality's NEPA regulations and the Board's environmental regulations at 49 CFR part 1105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OEA reviews the EISs and advises whether they meet CEQ and Board standards; the Board adopts OEA's conclusion that the specific Draft and Final Supplemental EISs at issue adequately assess impacts and satisfy regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106 NHPA consultation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106 of NHPA requires Federal agencies to 'take into account the effect of' undertakings on properties included in, or eligible for inclusion in, the National Register of Historic Places, to consult with the State Historic Preservation Officer (SHPO), and to afford the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation (ACHP) a reasonable opportunity to comment. If the undertaking would have an adverse effect, the agency must continue consultation to possibly mitigate the adverse effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board assesses whether Section 106 consultation occurred (SHPO, ACHP, MOA execution) and whether the consultation outcomes (MOA and amendments) satisfy 36 CFR 800.6(c). Execution and implementation of MOA terms can satisfy the agency's Section 106 obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) when effects are uncertain and for mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: When surveys are incomplete or the effects of an undertaking cannot be fully determined prior to approval, NHPA regulations allow development of an MOA that establishes responsibilities for the treatment of historic properties, implementation of mitigation measures, and ongoing consultation efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision notes that archaeological survey access restrictions left surveys incomplete and that an MOA can govern mitigation and responsibilities where adverse effects cannot be fully determined pre-approval. MOA amendments and filing with ACHP are part of satisfying Section 106.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption and imposition of mitigation measures (MMEP and MOA) as conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board adopts and imposes as conditions the environmental mitigation measures set forth in OEA's Environmental Memoranda and the Authority's Mitigation & Monitoring Enforcement Plan (MMEP), together with mitigation contained in the Section 106 MOA (as amended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MMEP specifies means to avoid, minimize, or mitigate harm; the Board conditions its exemption on compliance with the MMEP and MOA obligations. OEA recommended adopting and imposing these measures to satisfy NEPA and Section 106 obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OEA/Cooperating agency review and reliance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board relies on the Office of Environmental Analysis (OEA) as a cooperating agency and on OEA's independent analysis and Environmental Memoranda to assess whether the EISs and mitigation meet statutory and regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OEA's conclusions that substantive comments were incorporated, EISs adequately assess impacts, and that MOA/MMEP implementation satisfies Section 106 are adopted by the Board; OEA participation in MOA and filing with ACHP is treated as satisfying obligations under 36 CFR 800.6(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and evidentiary challenge requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board solicits public comment on transportation merits and environmental reviews; an absence of comments or a lack of evidentiary challenges in the record means prior findings on transportation merits and environmental conclusions are not overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In these proceedings the Board solicited comments on the CVY and LGA transportation merits and received none; the decision explains that because no party challenged the Board's earlier transportation conclusions or provided evidence to the contrary, those conclusions were reaffirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental justice and mitigation examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Where projects have substantial impacts on minority and low-income populations even after mitigation, mitigation measures may include installing sound barriers; acquiring property easements; locating suitable replacement properties and facilities; adding landscaping to screen structures, light, glare, and blocked views; and continued environmental justice outreach to refine mitigation during design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OEA and the Supplemental ROD identify environmental justice impacts and provide examples of mitigation techniques (MMEP Table references). Continued outreach is recommended to refine mitigation with community input.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to remove or adjust prior mitigation conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: OEA may recommend removing a mitigation measure from a prior decision if that measure pertains specifically to components replaced by a proposed modification (for example, removal of a pile-driving prohibition near a hospital that related to the component being replaced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board accepted OEA's recommendation to remove a previously imposed mitigation condition that no longer applied to the modified component, while adding other measures to assure compliance with final mitigation and Section 106 obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA conclusion criterion — conditioned action will not significantly impact environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may conclude that 'this action, as conditioned, will not significantly impact the quality of the human environment or the conservation of energy resources.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement functions as the Board's NEPA conclusion when it adopts EIS findings and imposes mitigation conditions; it supports issuing the exemption subject to those conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements — petitions for reconsideration and effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions include procedural directives such as publication notice, deadlines for petitions for reconsideration (e.g., must be filed by January 9, 2023), and the decision's effective date (effective on its service date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural rules govern post-decision challenges and administrative timelines and must be followed by parties seeking reconsideration.
